1/*!
2Reduces the size and coverage of OpenType fonts with TrueType or CFF outlines for embedding
3in PDFs. You can in general expect very good results in terms of font size, as most of the things
4that can be subsetted are also subsetted.
5
6# Scope
7**Note that the resulting font subsets will most likely be unusable in any other contexts than PDF writing,
8since a lot of information will be removed from the font which is not necessary in PDFs, but is
9necessary in other contexts.** This is on purpose, and for now, there are no plans to expand the
10scope of this crate to become a general purpose subsetter, as this is a massive undertaking and
11will make the already complex codebase even more complex.
12
13In the future,
14[klippa](https://github.com/googlefonts/fontations/tree/main/klippa) will hopefully fill the gap
15of a general-purpose subsetter in the Rust ecosystem.
16
17# Notes
18A couple of important notes if you want to use this crate in combination with your own pdf writer:
19
20- You must write your fonts as a CID font. This is because we remove the `cmap` table from the font,
21  so you must provide your own cmap table in the PDF.
22- Copyright information in the font will be retained.
23- When writing a CID font in PDF, CIDs must be used to address glyphs. This can be pretty tricky,
24  because the meaning of CID depends on the type of font you are embedding (see the PDF specification
25  for more information). The subsetter will convert SID-keyed fonts to CID-keyed ones and an identity
26  mapping from GID to CID for all fonts, regardless of the previous mapping. Because of this, you can
27  always use the remapped GID as the CID for a glyph, and do not need to worry about the type of font
28  you are embedding.
29
30# Example
31In the example below, we remove all glyphs except the ones with IDs 68, 69, 70 from Noto Sans.
32Those correspond to the letters 'a', 'b' and 'c'. We then save the resulting font to disk.
33
34```
35use subsetter::{subset, GlyphRemapper};
36
37# fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
38// Read the raw font data.
39let data = std::fs::read("fonts/NotoSans-Regular.ttf")?;
40
41// These are the glyphs we want to keep.
42let glyphs = &[68, 69, 70];
43
44// Create a new glyph remapper that remaps our glyphs to new glyph IDs. This is necessary because
45// glyph IDs in fonts must be consecutive. So if we only include the glyphs 68, 69, 70 and remove all
46// other glyph IDs, in the new font they will have the glyph IDs 1, 2, 3.
47let mut remapper = GlyphRemapper::new();
48for glyph in glyphs {
49    remapper.remap(*glyph);
50}
51
52// Create the subset.
53let sub = subset(&data, 0, &remapper)?;
54
55// This is how you can access the new glyph ID of a glyph in the old font.
56for glyph in glyphs {
57    println!("Glyph {} has the ID {} in the new font", *glyph, remapper.get(*glyph).unwrap());
58}
59
60// Write the resulting file.
61std::fs::write("target/Noto-Small.ttf", sub)?;
62# Ok(())
63# }
64```
65
66In the above example, the original font was 556 KB, while the
67resulting font is 1 KB.
68*/
69

101/// Subset the font face to include only the necessary glyphs and tables.
102///
103/// - The `data` must be in the OpenType font format.
104/// - The `index` is only relevant if the data contains a font collection
105///   (`.ttc` or `.otc` file). Otherwise, it should be 0.
106///
107/// CFF2 fonts are not supported.
108pub fn subset(data: &[u8], index: u32, mapper: &GlyphRemapper) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
109    subset_inner(data, index, &[], false, mapper)
110}
111
112/// Subset the font face to include only the necessary glyphs and tables, instantiated
113/// to the given variation coordinates.
114///
115/// This does the same as [`subset`], but allows you to specify variation coordinates.
116///
117/// It is important to note that if you pass a CFF2 font, it will be converted to a TrueType
118/// font.
119#[cfg(feature = "variable-fonts")]
120pub fn subset_with_variations(
121    data: &[u8],
122    index: u32,
123    variation_coordinates: &[(Tag, f32)],
124    mapper: &GlyphRemapper,
125) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
126    subset_inner(data, index, variation_coordinates, true, mapper)
127}
128
129fn subset_inner(
130    data: &[u8],
131    index: u32,
132    variation_coordinates: &[(Tag, f32)],
133    allow_cff2: bool,
134    mapper: &GlyphRemapper,
135) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
136    let mapper = mapper.clone();
137    let context =
138        prepare_context(data, index, variation_coordinates, allow_cff2, mapper)?;
139    _subset(context)
140}
141
142fn prepare_context<'a>(
143    data: &'a [u8],
144    index: u32,
145    #[cfg_attr(not(feature = "variable-fonts"), allow(unused))]
146    variation_coordinates: &[(Tag, f32)],
147    allow_cff2: bool,
148    mut gid_remapper: GlyphRemapper,
149) -> Result<Context<'a>> {
150    let face = parse(data, index)?;
151    let flavor = if face.table(Tag::GLYF).is_some() {
152        FontFlavor::TrueType
153    } else if face.table(Tag::CFF).is_some() {
154        FontFlavor::Cff
155    } else if face.table(Tag::CFF2).is_some() {
156        // Only works if `variable-fonts` feature is enabled, as we need skrifa
157        // so we can convert CFF2 into TrueType.
158        if allow_cff2 {
159            FontFlavor::Cff2
160        } else {
161            return Err(Unimplemented);
162        }
163    } else {
164        return Err(UnknownKind);
165    };
166
167    if flavor == FontFlavor::TrueType {
168        glyf::closure(&face, &mut gid_remapper)?;
169    }
170
171    let _ = variation_coordinates;
172
173    #[cfg(not(feature = "variable-fonts"))]
174    let interjector = Interjector::Dummy(PhantomData);
175    // For CFF, we _always_ want to do normal subsetting, since CFF cannot have variations.
176    // For TrueType, we prefer normal subsetting in case no variation was requested. If we do have
177    // variations, we use `skrifa` to instance.
178    // For CFF2, we _always_ use `skrifa` to instance.
179    #[cfg(feature = "variable-fonts")]
180    let interjector = if (variation_coordinates.is_empty()
181        && flavor == FontFlavor::TrueType)
182        || flavor == FontFlavor::Cff
183    {
184        // For TrueType and CFF, we are still best off using the normal subsetting logic in case no variation coordinates
185        // have been passed.
186        Interjector::Dummy(PhantomData)
187    } else {
188        Interjector::Skrifa(
189            interjector::skrifa::SkrifaInterjector::new(
190                data,
191                index,
192                variation_coordinates,
193            )
194            .ok_or(MalformedFont)?,
195        )
196    };
197
198    Ok(Context {
199        face,
200        mapper: gid_remapper,
201        interjector,
202        custom_maxp_data: None,
203        flavor,
204        tables: vec![],
205        long_loca: false,
206    })
207}
208
209fn _subset(mut ctx: Context) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
210    // See here for the required tables:
211    // https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/otff#required-tables
212    // but some of those are not strictly needed according to the PDF specification.
213
214    // Of the above tables, we are not including the following ones:
215    // - CFF2: Since we don't support CFF2
216    // - VORG: PDF doesn't use that table.
217    // - CMAP: CID fonts in PDF define their own cmaps, so we don't need to include them in the font.
218    // - GASP: Not mandated by PDF specification, and ghostscript also seems to exclude them.
219    // - OS2: Not mandated by PDF specification, and ghostscript also seems to exclude them.
220
221    if ctx.flavor == FontFlavor::TrueType {
222        // LOCA will be handled by GLYF
223        ctx.process(Tag::GLYF)?;
224        ctx.process(Tag::CVT)?; // won't be subsetted.
225        ctx.process(Tag::FPGM)?; // won't be subsetted.
226        ctx.process(Tag::PREP)?; // won't be subsetted.
227    } else if ctx.flavor == FontFlavor::Cff {
228        ctx.process(Tag::CFF)?;
229    } else if ctx.flavor == FontFlavor::Cff2 {
230        ctx.process(Tag::CFF2)?;
231    }
232
233    // Required tables.
234    ctx.process(Tag::HEAD)?;
235    ctx.process(Tag::HMTX)?;
236    ctx.process(Tag::MAXP)?;
237    // NAME is also not strictly needed, and ghostscript removes it when subsetting.
238    // However, it contains copyright information which probably should not be removed...
239    // Even though it can free up a lot of space for some fonts.
240    ctx.process(Tag::NAME)?;
241    ctx.process(Tag::POST)?;
242
243    Ok(construct(ctx))
244}

246/// Parse a font face from OpenType data.
247fn parse(data: &[u8], index: u32) -> Result<Face<'_>> {
248    let mut r = Reader::new(data);
249    let mut kind = r.read::<FontKind>().ok_or(UnknownKind)?;
250
251    // Parse font collection header if necessary.
252    if kind == FontKind::Collection {
253        r = Reader::new_at(data, 12 + 4 * (index as usize));
254        let offset = r.read::<u32>().ok_or(MalformedFont)?;
255        let subdata = data.get(offset as usize..).ok_or(MalformedFont)?;
256        r = Reader::new(subdata);
257        kind = r.read::<FontKind>().ok_or(MalformedFont)?;
258
259        // Cannot have nested collection
260        if kind == FontKind::Collection {
261            return Err(MalformedFont);
262        }
263    }
264
265    // Read number of table records.
266    let count = r.read::<u16>().ok_or(MalformedFont)?;
267    r.read::<u16>().ok_or(MalformedFont)?;
268    r.read::<u16>().ok_or(MalformedFont)?;
269    r.read::<u16>().ok_or(MalformedFont)?;
270
271    // Read table records.
272    let mut records = vec![];
273    for _ in 0..count {
274        records.push(r.read::<TableRecord>().ok_or(MalformedFont)?);
275    }
276
277    Ok(Face { data, records })
278}
279
280/// Construct a brand-new font.
281fn construct(mut ctx: Context) -> Vec<u8> {
282    ctx.tables.sort_by_key(|&(tag, _)| tag);
283
284    let mut w = Writer::new();
285    w.write(ctx.flavor);
286
287    // Write table directory.
288    let count = ctx.tables.len() as u16;
289    let entry_selector = (count as f32).log2().floor() as u16;
290    let search_range = 2u16.pow(u32::from(entry_selector)) * 16;
291    let range_shift = count * 16 - search_range;
292    w.write(count);
293    w.write(search_range);
294    w.write(entry_selector);
295    w.write(range_shift);
296
297    // This variable will hold the offset to the checksum adjustment field
298    // in the head table, which we'll have to write in the end (after
299    // checksumming the whole font).
300    let mut checksum_adjustment_offset = None;
301
302    // Write table records.
303    let mut offset = 12 + ctx.tables.len() * 16;
304    for (tag, data) in &mut ctx.tables {
305        if *tag == Tag::HEAD {
306            // Zero out checksum field in head table.
307            data.to_mut()[8..12].fill(0);
308            checksum_adjustment_offset = Some(offset + 8);
309        }
310
311        let len = data.len();
312        w.write(TableRecord {
313            tag: *tag,
314            checksum: checksum(data),
315            offset: offset as u32,
316            length: len as u32,
317        });
318
319        // Increase offset, plus padding zeros to align to 4 bytes.
320        offset += len;
321        while offset % 4 != 0 {
322            offset += 1;
323        }
324    }
325
326    // Write tables.
327    for (_, data) in &ctx.tables {
328        // Write data plus padding zeros to align to 4 bytes.
329        w.extend(data);
330        w.align(4);
331    }
332
333    // Write checksum adjustment field in head table.
334    let mut data = w.finish();
335    if let Some(i) = checksum_adjustment_offset {
336        let sum = checksum(&data);
337        let val = 0xB1B0AFBA_u32.wrapping_sub(sum);
338        data[i..i + 4].copy_from_slice(&val.to_be_bytes());
339    }
340
341    data
342}
343
344/// Calculate a checksum over the sliced data as a sum of u32s. If the data
345/// length is not a multiple of four, it is treated as if padded with zero to a
346/// length that is a multiple of four.
347fn checksum(data: &[u8]) -> u32 {
348    let mut sum = 0u32;
349    for chunk in data.chunks(4) {
350        let mut bytes = [0; 4];
351        bytes[..chunk.len()].copy_from_slice(chunk);
352        sum = sum.wrapping_add(u32::from_be_bytes(bytes));
353    }
354    sum
355}

357/// Subsetting context.
358struct Context<'a> {
359    /// Original face.
360    face: Face<'a>,
361    /// A map from old gids to new gids, and the reverse
362    mapper: GlyphRemapper,
363    /// The font flavor.
364    flavor: FontFlavor,
365    /// Subsetted tables.
366    tables: Vec<(Tag, Cow<'a, [u8]>)>,
367    /// An object that can _interject_ data during the subsetting process.
368    /// Normally, when subsetting CFF/TrueType fonts, we will simply read the corresponding
369    /// data from the old font and rewrite it to the new font, for example when writing the
370    /// `hmtx` table.
371    ///
372    /// However, in case we are subsetting with variation coordinates, we instead rely on skrifa
373    /// to apply the variation coordinates and interject that data during the subsetting process
374    /// instead of using the data from the old font.
375    interjector: Interjector<'a>,
376    /// Custom data that should be used for writing the `maxp` table. Only needed for CFF2,
377    /// where we need to synthesize a V1 table after converting.
378    pub(crate) custom_maxp_data: Option<MaxpData>,
379    /// Whether the long loca format was chosen.
380    long_loca: bool,
381}
382
383impl<'a> Context<'a> {
384    /// Expect a table.
385    fn expect_table(&self, tag: Tag) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
386        self.face.table(tag)
387    }
388
389    /// Process a table.
390    fn process(&mut self, tag: Tag) -> Result<()> {
391        let data = match self.face.table(tag) {
392            Some(data) => data,
393            None => return Ok(()),
394        };
395
396        match tag {
397            Tag::GLYF => glyf::subset(self)?,
398            Tag::LOCA => panic!("handled by glyf"),
399            Tag::CFF => cff::subset(self)?,
400            #[cfg(feature = "variable-fonts")]
401            Tag::CFF2 => cff2::subset(self)?,
402            #[cfg(not(feature = "variable-fonts"))]
403            Tag::CFF2 => return Err(Unimplemented),
404            Tag::HEAD => head::subset(self)?,
405            Tag::HHEA => panic!("handled by hmtx"),
406            Tag::HMTX => hmtx::subset(self)?,
407            Tag::POST => post::subset(self)?,
408            Tag::MAXP => maxp::subset(self)?,
409            Tag::NAME => name::subset(self)?,
410            _ => self.push(tag, data),
411        }
412
413        Ok(())
414    }
415
416    /// Push a subsetted table.
417    fn push(&mut self, tag: Tag, table: impl Into<Cow<'a, [u8]>>) {
418        debug_assert!(
419            !self.tables.iter().any(|&(prev, _)| prev == tag),
420            "duplicate {tag} table"
421        );
422        self.tables.push((tag, table.into()));
423    }
424}
425
426/// A font face with OpenType tables.
427struct Face<'a> {
428    data: &'a [u8],
429    records: Vec<TableRecord>,
430}
431
432impl<'a> Face<'a> {
433    fn table(&self, tag: Tag) -> Option<&'a [u8]> {
434        let i = self.records.binary_search_by(|record| record.tag.cmp(&tag)).ok()?;
435        let record = self.records.get(i)?;
436        let start = record.offset as usize;
437        let end = start + (record.length as usize);
438        self.data.get(start..end)
439    }
440}

442/// Whether the font is a font collection or a single font.
443#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, Eq, PartialEq)]
444enum FontKind {
445    /// A font collection.
446    Collection,
447    /// A single font.
448    Single,
449}
450
451impl Readable<'_> for FontKind {
452    const SIZE: usize = u32::SIZE;
453
454    fn read(r: &mut Reader) -> Option<Self> {
455        match r.read::<u32>()? {
456            // TrueType
457            0x00010000 | 0x74727565 => Some(FontKind::Single),
458            // CFF
459            0x4F54544F => Some(FontKind::Single),
460            0x74746366 => Some(FontKind::Collection),
461            _ => None,
462        }
463    }
464}
465
466#[derive(PartialEq, Eq, Debug, Copy, Clone)]
467/// The flavor of outlines used by the font.
468enum FontFlavor {
469    /// TrueType fonts using the `glyf` table.
470    TrueType,
471    /// CFF fonts using the `CFF` table.
472    Cff,
473    /// CFF2 fonts using the `CFF2` table.
474    Cff2,
475}
476
477impl Writeable for FontFlavor {
478    fn write(&self, w: &mut Writer) {
479        w.write::<u32>(match self {
480            // Important note: This is the magic for TrueType and not CFF2.
481            // However, CFF2 fonts will be converted to TrueType as part of the subsetting
482            // process, hence we write the same magic.
483            FontFlavor::TrueType | FontFlavor::Cff2 => 0x00010000,
484            FontFlavor::Cff => 0x4F54544F,
485        })
486    }
487}

489/// A 4-byte OpenType tag.
490#[derive(Copy, Clone, Eq, PartialEq, Ord, PartialOrd, Hash)]
491pub struct Tag([u8; 4]);
492
493impl Tag {
494    /// Create a new tag.
495    pub fn new(tag: &[u8; 4]) -> Self {
496        Self(*tag)
497    }
498
499    /// Return the value of the tag.
500    pub fn get(&self) -> &[u8; 4] {
501        &self.0
502    }
503}
504
505impl FromStr for Tag {
506    type Err = TryFromSliceError;
507
508    /// Tries to create a new tag from a string.
509    ///
510    /// Return `Err(_)` if the string is not 4 bytes in size.
511    fn from_str(s: &str) -> std::result::Result<Self, Self::Err> {
512        s.as_bytes().try_into().map(Self)
513    }
514}

579/// Locates a table in the font file.
580#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, Eq, PartialEq)]
581struct TableRecord {
582    tag: Tag,
583    checksum: u32,
584    offset: u32,
585    length: u32,
586}
587
588impl Readable<'_> for TableRecord {
589    const SIZE: usize = Tag::SIZE + u32::SIZE + u32::SIZE + u32::SIZE;
590
591    fn read(r: &mut Reader) -> Option<Self> {
592        Some(TableRecord {
593            tag: r.read::<Tag>()?,
594            checksum: r.read::<u32>()?,
595            offset: r.read::<u32>()?,
596            length: r.read::<u32>()?,
597        })
598    }
599}
600
601impl Writeable for TableRecord {
602    fn write(&self, w: &mut Writer) {
603        w.write::<Tag>(self.tag);
604        w.write::<u32>(self.checksum);
605        w.write::<u32>(self.offset);
606        w.write::<u32>(self.length);
607    }
608}

627/// The result type for everything.
628type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, Error>;
629
630/// Parsing failed because the font face is malformed.
631#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, Eq, PartialEq)]
632pub enum Error {
633    /// The file contains an unknown kind of font.
634    UnknownKind,
635    /// The font is malformed (or there is a bug in the font parsing logic).
636    MalformedFont,
637    /// The font relies on an unimplemented feature, and thus the subsetting
638    /// process couldn't be completed.
639    Unimplemented,
640    /// An unexpected error occurred when subsetting the font. Indicates that there
641    /// is a logical bug in the subsetter.
642    SubsetError,
643    /// An overflow occurred during the computation. Could be either an issue
644    /// with the font itself, or a bug in the subsetter logic.
645    OverflowError,
646    /// An error occurred while processing the CFF table.
647    CFFError,
648}
649
650impl Display for Error {
651    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
652        match self {
653            Self::UnknownKind => f.write_str("unknown font kind"),
654            Self::MalformedFont => f.write_str("malformed font"),
655            Self::Unimplemented => f.write_str("unsupported feature in font"),
656            Self::SubsetError => f.write_str("subsetting of font failed"),
657            Self::OverflowError => f.write_str("overflow occurred"),
658            Self::CFFError => f.write_str("processing CFF table failed"),
659        }
660    }
661}
662
663impl std::error::Error for Error {}
